stories.title: Torrance Site Featured in 2026 CREDA SoCal Real Estate Challenge
stories.excerpt: Now in its 29th year, the CREDA SoCal UCLA vs. USC Real Estate Challenge will be held Nov. 19 on the UCLA campus. Each year, the competition pits a five-member graduate student team from the Ziman Center of Real Estate at UCLA’s Anderson School of Business against a five member graduate student team from the Lusk Center at USC’s Marshall School of Business and Price School of Public Policy to determine the highest and best use for a unique parcel of land in Southern California. The two universities are currently tied at 14 wins apiece. For 2026, the competition will be an approximately 30-acre site in the City of Torrance utilized as the city’s Civic Center, which includes City Hall, a municipal pool, a cultural arts center, a library and police department. The City wants to revitalize its Civic Center to better utilize the property by consolidating the public uses and developing the remaining acreage. “This is a great infill site that provides a fantastic opportunity for creativity,” said Erin Crum, EVP, asset management, Alere Property, and LA Real Estate Challenge Chair. “That is why the CREDA SoCal challenge is so valuable for these students. They can talk to experts, experiment, collaborate and work on solving a real-world challenge that will also provide valuable insight to the city. I look forward to seeing what the students present.” The post Torrance Site Featured in 2026 CREDA SoCal Real Estate Challenge appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Torrance Civic Center, ~30 acres, targeted for consolidation and mixed-use redevelopment
UCLA Anderson vs. USC Marshall compete Nov. 2026 to determine highest-and-best use
City seeks to unlock value by consolidating public uses and densifying surplus land
stories.summary: The City of Torrance is using a 2026 graduate real estate competition to explore redevelopment options for its 30-acre Civic Center in Southern California. The site currently houses City Hall, a municipal pool, cultural arts center, library, and police department. The city plans to consolidate these municipal functions to free acreage for private development. UCLA Anderson and USC Marshall teams will present alternative concepts to guide the city's revitalization strategy.
stories.impact: Signals near-term entitlement and zoning clarity for a major infill site in the South Bay LA market. If the city pursues densification (mixed-use or multifamily), this represents a rare institutional land conversion opportunity; developers tracking LA coastal submarket supply constraints should monitor Torrance's disposition timeline and density assumptions, which will influence feasibility and competitive positioning for rental housing in a supply-constrained pocket.

stories.title: Coworking Provider Nomadworks Leases Three Floors with Koeppel Rosen
stories.excerpt: Koeppel Rosen LLC, leasing and management agent for the Rosen family portfolio, said Wednesday that Nomadworks has signed a new 16-year, two-month lease totaling 33,783 rentable square feet at 122 W. 27th St. in Manhattan. The lease covers the building’s entire ninth, 10th and 11th floors, which will be transformed into a new coworking location for Nomadworks. Nomadworks is a New York City-based coworking and flexible office space provider offering private offices, shared workspaces, meeting rooms, and workplace amenities for businesses, entrepreneurs, and remote professionals. Max Koeppel, director of leasing at Koeppel Rosen, represented ownership in-house. LSL Advisors represented the tenant. “Koeppel Rosen is pleased to welcome Nomadworks to 122 W. 27th St. and to have secured such a long-term commitment for the building,” said Koeppel. “The lease at 122 W. 27th St. expands the Nomadworks presence in Manhattan and reflects the continued demand for flexible workspace throughout the city.” The post Coworking Provider Nomadworks Leases Three Floors with Koeppel Rosen appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Nomadworks leased 33,783 sf, three full floors, 16+ years at 122 W. 27th St., Manhattan
Long-term flex office commitment signals sustained demand for coworking in NYC
Flex workspace provider expanding footprint; reflects post-pandemic hybrid work normalization
stories.summary: Coworking provider Nomadworks signed a 16-year-plus lease for 33,783 square feet (floors 9–11) at 122 W. 27th St. in Manhattan's Flatiron/Chelsea submarket. The lease represents a long-term, full-floor commitment by a flex office operator. Koeppel Rosen secured the deal, noting continued strong demand for flexible workspace throughout Manhattan.
stories.impact: Limited direct impact on multifamily. Long-term flex office leasing does not pressure residential supply or demand; if anything, sustained coworking demand signals office-to-residential conversion risk is lower than feared. However, the lease anchors office demand in Chelsea, which could modestly support adjacent retail and F&B, benefiting mixed-use projects but not rental apartment fundamentals.

stories.title: Gantry Arranges $110M Refi for Bixby Capital Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Gantry has secured a $110-million permanent loan to refinance a six-property portfolio for Bixby Capital Management. The portfolio includes five single-tenant industrial assets in Southern California and Texas submarkets and Bixby’s headquarters office building in Newport Beach. All six assets are 100% leased. Senior director Stephan Coste, principal Andy Bratt and associate Nick Severson of Gantry’s Irvine production office, represented the borrower. The 12-year, fixed-rate, non-recourse loan was secured from one of Gantry’s long-time correspondent insurance company lenders and features full-term interest-only. Gantry will service the loan. The loan’s flexible structure gives Bixby the freedom to adjust its portfolio over time while keeping its long-term financing in place. Tailored collateral flexibility supports Bixby’s long-term portfolio strategy. Coste said, “Insurance company correspondents remain a time-tested source of permanent debt in any cycle. We evaluated more than 40 options to find the right structure and the right partner to maximize proceeds for this high-quality, fully leased portfolio.” The post Gantry Arranges $110M Refi for Bixby Capital Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Gantry closed $110M permanent refi for six-property industrial + office portfolio, 100% leased
12-year fixed-rate, interest-only, non-recourse; insurance company lender; full-term flexibility
SoCal and Texas industrial assets plus Newport Beach HQ; demonstrates insurance capital availability
stories.summary: Gantry arranged a $110 million permanent refinancing for Bixby Capital Management's six-property portfolio: five single-tenant industrial assets across Southern California and Texas, plus Bixby's Newport Beach headquarters office building. The 12-year, fixed-rate, non-recourse loan features full-term interest-only and was secured from an insurance company correspondent lender. The flexible structure allows Bixby to adjust its portfolio while maintaining long-term financing.
stories.impact: Demonstrates sustained insurance company appetite for industrial and fully leased assets in high-barrier-to-entry SoCal and Texas markets. Signals permanent capital availability and non-recourse terms remain viable, supporting development feasibility for industrial and mixed-use projects in these submarkets. No direct multifamily signal, but affirms capital markets are functioning for core real estate.

stories.title: Related Adds Goddard School Franchise to Village at Tuxedo Reserve
stories.excerpt: Related Companies’ The Village at Tuxedo Reserve is set to open a new location of The Goddard School, a nationally acclaimed early childhood education franchise, in New York’s Hudson Valley in fall 2027. The 10,000-square-foot early childhood education center in Tuxedo, NY will sit on a two-acre landscaped lot, with 5,000 square feet of surrounding play yards and dedicated adjacent parking. “The Goddard School is one of the most trusted names in daycare and early childhood education, and will seamlessly complement the strong educational network already serving the area,” said Greg Gushee, EVP at Related Companies. “We are thrilled to welcome The Goddard School of Tuxedo as a new resource for residents and the broader community.” Surrounding the school, The Village will offer families access to shopping, dining, wellness, and year-round community programming. The Village is anchored by Market Square, which features a timber-framed destination food market; and The Village Green, which will serve as a hub for family-friendly events. The post Related Adds Goddard School Franchise to Village at Tuxedo Reserve appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Related Companies' Village at Tuxedo Reserve adds Goddard School early childhood center, 10,000 sf
Opening fall 2027 in Hudson Valley, NY; 2-acre landscaped site with dedicated parking and play yards
Amenity anchor for master-planned mixed-use community targeting families and residents
stories.summary: Related Companies is adding a 10,000-square-foot Goddard School early childhood education franchise to The Village at Tuxedo Reserve in Tuxedo, New York (Hudson Valley). The facility will open fall 2027 on a two-acre site with 5,000 square feet of play yards and dedicated parking. The school is positioned as a key family-focused amenity within the broader village development, which includes Market Square, dining, retail, and The Village Green event hub.
stories.impact: Signals Related's strategic focus on amenity-rich, family-oriented mixed-use development in exurban/suburban Hudson Valley markets. The inclusion of on-site early childhood education is a competitive differentiator for attracting young families and increasing renter stickiness in Tuxedo; developers competing in similar exurban Hudson Valley or Westchester markets should expect family-targeted amenities (daycare, schools, parks) to become table-stakes in lease-up strategy and rent justification.

stories.title: WinnCompanies Lines Up Financing for Mixed-Income Salem TOD
stories.excerpt: WinnCompanies has secured financing for a long-awaited, 115-unit, mixed-income apartment building designed to revitalize the northern gateway to downtown Salem, MA. To be named The Exchange Salem, the seven-story building will be erected on the site of a former municipal parking lot overlooking the city’s mass transit station and parking garage. The $48-million construction project will offer 20 studios, 60 one-bedroom units and 35 two-bedroom units. Of the 115 apartments, 55 will be available to households earning up to 60% of Area Median Income; 22 will be available at incomes up to 30% AMI; 20 will serve middle-income households; and 18 will be rented at market rates. “This project will deliver long-held public and economic goals for the City of Salem, creating housing local workers can afford and improving the public realm connecting North Salem and the city’s downtown,” said WinnDevelopment president Adam Stein. “This milestone is truly result of a team effort, and we are grateful to all the public and private partners who persevered alongside us.” The post WinnCompanies Lines Up Financing for Mixed-Income Salem TOD appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: WinnCompanies financed $48M, 115-unit mixed-income TOD in Salem, MA; 55 units at ≤60% AMI, 22 at ≤30% AMI
Seven-story building on former municipal parking lot; transit-adjacent to mass transit station and downtown
20 studios, 60 one-bedroom, 35 two-bedroom; 18 at market rate; strong public-private partnership delivery
stories.summary: WinnCompanies secured financing for The Exchange Salem, a $48 million, 115-unit mixed-income apartment building in downtown Salem, Massachusetts. The seven-story development sits on a former municipal parking lot overlooking the city's mass transit station. Units include 55 at ≤60% AMI, 22 at ≤30% AMI, 20 at middle-income, and 18 at market rate; the mix spans studios to two-bedrooms. The project addresses long-standing city goals for affordable housing and downtown revitalization.
stories.impact: Demonstrates strong capital availability and public appetite for mixed-income TOD in secondary Northeast markets. Salem's transit-adjacent positioning and mixed-income subsidy structure (likely state/local tax credits and gap financing) set a template for similar secondary-market gateway cities. Developers should track Salem's lease-up absorption and affordability stack as a comp for New England TOD feasibility; the success here will inform underwriting for similar transit-proximate, mixed-income plays in Worcester, Providence, and similar markets.

stories.title: Delivery Service Spot & Tango, Ad Firm MediaRadar Sign at 11 Bryant Park Plaza
stories.excerpt: Two companies have signed for close to 32,000 square feet of office space at 11 Bryant Park Plaza. Dog food delivery service Spot & Tango took 15,931 square feet on the entire seventh floor of the Midtown office building, while advertising intelligence firm MediaRadar moved from a sublease at the property to a direct deal with 15,931 square feet on the eighth floor, according to landlord broker CBRE. Both deals were for a term of five years, and asking rent in the building owned by AM Property Holdings, Axonic Capital and Eyn Holdings was $75 to $95 per square foot, according to CBRE. “The leasing activity demonstrates strong demand for well-located buildings that combine character, convenience and modern amenities,” CBRE’s Neil King, who represented the landlords alongside Paul Amrich, Conor Kenny and Matthew Dichter, said in a statement. Skylight Leasing’s Elie Reiss negotiated on behalf of Spot & Tango, while Evan Algier and Nick Masi of Cushman & Wakefield handled the deal for MediaRadar. Reiss did not immediately respond to a request for comment and C&W declined to comment. An undisclosed fintech company also signed a 16,183-square-foot lease on the 15th floor of the 22-story building, with Elliot Zellinger of Savitt Partners representing the firm. Zellinger declined to provide the name of the tenant. The owning joint venture acquired the property, with an alternate address of 114 West 41st Street, in November 2025 for $133 million from Clarion Partners. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Spot & Tango (pet food delivery) leased 15,931 sf, entire 7th floor, 5 years at 11 Bryant Park Plaza, Manhattan
MediaRadar (ad intelligence) moved from sublease to direct deal: 15,931 sf, 8th floor, 5 years
Asking rent $75–$95 psf; both tenants signed for ~32,000 sf total; strong office demand signal in Midtown
stories.summary: Two companies signed leases totaling nearly 32,000 square feet at 11 Bryant Park Plaza in Midtown Manhattan. Pet food delivery service Spot & Tango leased the entire seventh floor (15,931 sf) for five years, while advertising intelligence firm MediaRadar moved from a sublease to a direct deal for the eighth floor (15,931 sf), also five years. Asking rents ranged from $75 to $95 per square foot. Both deals reflect strong demand for well-amenitized, well-located Midtown office buildings.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance. Office leasing activity in Midtown confirms that core office demand persists for quality buildings in Manhattan's premier submarkets. Does not signal residential demand pressures; may even indicate reduced office-to-residential conversion urgency in trophy Midtown properties, reducing supply risk for nearby multifamily but not driving incremental apartment demand.

stories.title: 13th Floor Sells Florida Housing Community for $29M
stories.excerpt: 13th Floor Investments has sold a new housing community designated for residents 55 years and older in West Delray Beach, Fla., for $29.3 million, property records show. Robbins Property Associates purchased the 7.6-acre asset called Solera at Avalon Trails. The community features 74 single-story houses at 14800 Cumberland Drive, about a mile west of the South Jog Road. “Our vision was to deliver a thoughtfully designed community that responded to the evolving needs of active adults who value the flexibility of renting, maintenance-free lifestyle and access to a full suite of amenities,” Mike Nunziata, president 13th Floor Investments’s 13th Floor Homes division, said in a statement. Walker & Dunlop’s Still Hunter represented the Miami-based developer, which completed the development in 2024, a year after securing a $14.1 million construction loan from CIBC Bank. The two- and three-bedroom villas range in size from about 1,300 to 1,450 square feet. Berkadia originated a $19.2 million, fixed-rate acquisition loan for Robbins Property Associates. The brokerage’s Mitch Sinberg, Brad Williamson, Scott Wadler and Hugo Hernandez arranged the 10-year, Freddie Mac-backed loan. The Tampa-based buyer owns two multifamily properties in South Florida. The region has seen an uptick in senior housing sales in recent months. In August, PGIM Real Estate offloaded a relatively new assisted living facility, also in Delray Beach, for at least $140 million. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: 13th Floor Homes sold Solera at Avalon Trails (74 rental villas, 55+), West Delray Beach, for $29.3M
Robbins Property Associates acquired 7.6-acre asset; completed 2024 after $14.1M construction loan from CIBC
Berkadia provided $19.2M fixed-rate acquisition loan for buyer; two-three-bedroom villas, 1,300–1,450 sf range
stories.summary: 13th Floor Investments sold Solera at Avalon Trails, a 74-unit rental villa community for seniors 55+ in West Delray Beach, Florida, to Robbins Property Associates for $29.3 million. The 7.6-acre property was completed in 2024 following a $14.1 million construction loan from CIBC. Unit sizes range from 1,300 to 1,450 square feet (two to three bedrooms). Berkadia originated a $19.2 million fixed-rate acquisition loan for the buyer.
stories.impact: Signals strong acquisition appetite and debt availability for stabilized senior rental communities in South Florida. The ~$396K per unit sale price and ~1.5x construction cost premium reflect robust buyer demand for operational 55+ rental communities. Demonstrates capital stack durability for this asset class; developers underwriting senior housing in high-growth Florida submarkets (Delray, Boca, Miami-Dade) should expect continued institutional buyer competition and supportive debt markets, supporting development feasibility and potential exit strategies.

stories.title: ESRT Faces New Activist Investor Following Stake Acquisition
stories.excerpt: An activist shareholder has arrived at Empire State Building Trust (ESRT). Erez Asset Management, a New Rochelle, N.Y.-based activist investment firm and hedge fund manager, has disclosed its acquisition of 10 million shares, or a 5.8 percent stake, in ESRT, Bisnow first reported. Erez has already begun putting pressure on ESRT leadership to sell some or all of its 8 million-square-foot Manhattan portfolio, Crain’s New York reported, which includes the Empire State Building, 1400 Broadway and 1 Grand Central Place. The acquisition by Erez is likely unwelcome news for Tony Malkin, ESRT’s CEO and controlling shareholder. Shares in the New York-based real estate investment trust (REIT), currently one of New York’s largest landlords, have lost nearly 60 percent of their value over the past two years. They currently trade at around $4.40 per share. Erez plans to have discussions with ESRT’s management and board members about governance, corporate structure, compensations and financial decisions, according to its Securities Exchange Commission (SEC) filing. Erez is managed by Bruce Schanzer, the former CEO of Cedar Realty Trust. Undervalued, small-capitalization real estate stocks are the firm’s speciality. Erez said in its filing that it believes ESRT’s portfolio is undervalued — a common refrain in the world of REITs, although many others have enjoyed some recovery of values this year. ESRT, on the other hand, has seen its market capitalization decline from $3.3 billion in 2024 to just $1.3 billion in recent months. Multiple quarters of earnings calls by ESRT leadership dwelled on declining visits to the Empire State Building’s observatory, largely linked to persistent drops in international tourism. The iconic destination is also contending with new competition from viewing platforms at One Vanderbilt and at Hudson Yards towers. The observatory generated $12.4 million of net operating income in the second quarter of this year, a sharp 48.5 percent decrease from $24.1 m
bullets: Erez Asset Management acquired 5.8% stake (10M shares) in Empire State Realty Trust (ESRT); activist push underway
ESRT shares down ~60% in 2 years; currently $4.40/share; Erez pressuring leadership to sell portfolio or assets
ESRT portfolio: 8M sf Manhattan office including Empire State Building, 1400 Broadway, 1 Grand Central Place
stories.summary: Activist hedge fund Erez Asset Management disclosed a 5.8 percent stake (10 million shares) in Empire State Realty Trust and has begun pressuring ESRT leadership to sell some or all of its 8 million-square-foot Manhattan office portfolio. ESRT stock has lost nearly 60 percent of its value over two years and currently trades at $4.40 per share. The portfolio includes landmark properties like the Empire State Building, 1400 Broadway, and 1 Grand Central Place.
stories.impact: Signals potential portfolio dislocation and distress dynamics among Manhattan office REITs. If ESRT divests trophy office assets at fire-sale valuations, it may depress commercial real estate pricing, tighten credit availability, and trigger CMBS losses that ripple through capital markets. Multifamily developers should monitor ESRT's financing and asset sales closely: office-to-residential conversion opportunities may emerge if trophy Manhattan office properties become underfunded or distressed, and lender stress could tighten multifamily credit availability industry-wide.

stories.title: Citigroup Supplies $28M Refi for Revived Office Building in Arlington, Va.
stories.excerpt: A Washington, D.C., developer has secured fresh capital to continue engineering the turnaround of a once-struggling office building just across the Potomac River. Jemal Equities, which is run by Douglas Development Managing Principal Matthew Jemal, has landed a $28 million commercial mortgage-backed securities loan to refinance its 10-story office property at 1530 Wilson Boulevard, in Arlington, Va., Commercial Observer has learned. Citigroup provided the loan for the roughly 174,000-square-foot building in Arlington’s Rosslyn neighborhood that Jemal Equities acquired in October 2025 for $28 million from Velocis when it was 61 percent leased. The 1990-built property is now 89 percent leased with a 6.8-year weighted average lease term (WALT) compared to a 2.8 WALT at the time of purchase, according to Meridian Capital Group, which arranged the loan. Meridian’s Cary Pollack and Judah Neuman negotiated the debt. “Matthew Jemal has built a reputation for turning buildings around, and 1530 Wilson is the latest example,” Pollack said in a statement. “What Jemal Equities accomplished here in under a year comes down to grit, hard work and determination. Citi recognized the strength of that execution, and we were able to secure financing that reflects where this building is today and where it’s headed.” The $28 million acquisition by Jemal marked a 61 percent drop from the $71.4 million Velocis paid for the building in April 2020. Recent upgrades include a renovated lobby, an outdoor terrace and a fitness center with locker rooms. A 50-person conference center is under development. Anchor tenants at 1530 Wilson include Lincoln Property Company, Blue Origin and SAS Institute. Citigroup and Jemal Equities did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com
bullets: Jemal Equities secured $28M CMBS refi via Citigroup for 1530 Wilson Boulevard, Arlington, VA office
Property 174,000 sf, 10-story; purchased Oct. 2025 at 61% leased; now 89% leased, 6.8-year WALT
Improved credit profile and debt availability signal office turnaround feasibility in DC-area submarkets
stories.summary: Jemal Equities, led by Matthew Jemal, secured a $28 million CMBS refinancing from Citigroup for its 10-story, 174,000-square-foot office building at 1530 Wilson Boulevard in Arlington, Virginia (Rosslyn submarket). Jemal acquired the property in October 2025 when it was 61 percent leased; it is now 89 percent leased with a 6.8-year weighted average lease term, up from 2.8 years at purchase. Meridian Capital arranged the loan.
stories.impact: Demonstrates capital market appetite for stabilized office repositioning in DC-area submarkets, particularly Rosslyn/Arlington. The rapid leasing improvement (61% to 89%) and debt refinancing signal that selective office markets outside core Manhattan remain viable. Multifamily developers in Arlington/DC should note: office stabilization in Rosslyn may reduce short-term conversion opportunities but signals workforce retention and tenant demand, supporting demand drivers for nearby multifamily and mixed-use TOD projects.

stories.title: Three Fashion Tenants Ink Deals at 231 West 39th Street
stories.excerpt: Three women’s apparel brands have taken office and showroom space at 231 West 39th Street in Manhattan’s Garment District, landlord broker and building manager Adams & Company announced Wednesday. Rino & Pelle, a Netherlands-based women’s fashion and accessories brand, has inked a 3,332-square-foot lease at the 12-story building, while luxury women’s wear and fine jewelry brand Valentina Kova took 1,594 square feet, and ready-to-wear resort attire retailer Sister NY scooped up 900 square feet at the property. The length of each lease and the asking rents were not disclosed. The average asking rent for office space in Midtown was $85.08 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026, according to Colliers data. The average asking rent for retail space in nearby Herald Square was $403 per square foot in the third quarter, according to CBRE data. Jeff Buslik from Adams & Company represented the landlord, 231/249 West 39 Street Associates, in all three deals. The tenant brokers were not immediately disclosed. “231 West 39th Street has long served as a destination for apparel brands, designers and manufacturers, and this growing roster of fashion tenants reflects the continued demand for well-located office and showroom space in Manhattan’s Garment District,” Buslik said in a statement. “With more than 85 fashion showrooms in the building, we continue to see companies looking for space that supports both their creative and business operations, while offering the accessibility and amenities of a central Midtown location,” Buslik added. Constructed in 1901, 231 West 39th Street is between Seventh and Eighth avenues. Other tenants in the building include apparel, accessory design and manufacturing company Decor Global, as well as apparel firm Akoo Clothing. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Three women's fashion brands signed at 231 West 39th Street, Manhattan Garment District; ~5,826 sf combined
Rino & Pelle (Netherlands-based), Valentina Kova (luxury), Sister NY (resort wear) took office and showroom space
Lease terms and rents undisclosed; signals Garment District retail/showroom demand persistence
stories.summary: Three women's apparel brands leased space at 231 West 39th Street in Manhattan's Garment District: Rino & Pelle (Netherlands fashion/accessories, 3,332 sf), Valentina Kova (luxury wear and fine jewelry, 1,594 sf), and Sister NY (resort attire, 900 sf). Combined leasing totaled approximately 5,826 square feet. Lease terms and rents were not disclosed. The deals reflect continued demand for showroom and office space in the Garment District.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Garment District office and showroom leasing signals the neighborhood retains niche demand from fashion brands seeking low-cost space and industry clustering. This does not materially affect residential supply or demand; however, it suggests Garment District commercial rents remain attractive, reducing conversion pressure on multifamily developers. No broader rent or development implications for apartment markets.
